description: An operator-counting heuristic gives each operator a count `Y_o ≥ 0` and minimizes the total cost `Σ cost(o) · Y_o` with a linear program (*LP*). Each constraint is true for the operator counts of every plan, so the minimum never overestimates (it is *admissible*). The crate uses two kinds of constraints: the *state equation*, which balances how often a plan can make each fact true and false, and the LM-cut landmarks, where each cut must be used at least once. An infeasible LP proves a dead end. It is a strong heuristic for optimal search, but each state needs one LP solve (feature `lp`).

papers.authors: Florian Pommerening, Gabriele Röger, Malte Helmert, Blai Bonet
papers.title: LP-Based Heuristics for Cost-Optimal Planning
papers.venue: International Conference on Automated Planning and Scheduling (ICAPS)
